subject: Interview with Councilor Zac Bears
overview: Medford City Councilor Zac Bears joined the Medford Bytes podcast to review his first four years in office and outline his re-election platform. He discussed municipal budget challenges, comprehensive zoning reform, balance-of-power issues in the city charter, and his campaign activities.

items.title: Podcast Introduction and Favorite Local Restaurant
items.summary: Danielle Balocca and Chelli Keshavan opened the episode, and guest Zac Bears shared that Colleen's is his favorite spot to eat in Medford.

items.title: Reflections on First Four Years on City Council
items.summary: Zac Bears reflected on his past two terms, highlighting pandemic response efforts, council rule modernizations, ordinance passages, zoning recodification, and budget transparency.

items.title: Zoning Recodification and Economic Impact
items.summary: Zac Bears explained that updating zoning regulations sets conditions to attract future private investment and commercial growth, providing long-term revenue for city services.

items.title: Municipal Budget and Revenue Requirements
items.summary: Zac Bears emphasized that Medford needs $30 million to $40 million in new annual revenue to fund school facilities, street maintenance, municipal staffing, and capital projects.

items.title: City Charter and Government Structure
items.summary: Zac Bears discussed the concentration of executive authority under the current city charter and explained council proposals to allow budget amendments, appointment confirmations, and independent council staff.

items.title: Third-Term Priorities and Campaign Info
items.summary: Zac Bears outlined his key goals for a third term—including complete zoning reform, reviewing the Charter Study Committee's draft, and securing long-term capital funding—and shared details about his re-election campaign.
